title: Unify transport-layer interfaces and advance deprecation path for client SDKs
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Centralize the client transport abstraction across Python/JS/Go SDKs so we can: (1) ship coordinated minor/patch bumps with a consistent retry/backoff and observability surface, (2) remove three deprecated per-language transport parameters that diverged historically, and (3) provide a clear non-breaking migration path for customers.
acceptance_criteria: A language-agnostic Transport interface is implemented in each SDK with identical semantic guarantees (request/response shape, retry/backoff hooks, metrics hooks).
Existing public constructors that accepted transport-specific kwargs are deprecated with clear runtime warnings; a compatibility shim is provided for one minor release.
Automated translation tests (golden-record style) validate parity across Python/JS/Go for the streaming and non-streaming code paths.
Performance regressions are <5% p50 latency and token cost delta is within noise on representative workloads.
Release notes + migration guide published; a migration checker script exists to detect removed params in downstream repos.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — implemented prototype Transport interface in python-sdk (local branch: prot/transport-unify). Observed a 3% p50 latency improvement for small-batch streaming due to centralizing connection reuse.

2026-03-04: Design review with client-eng and dev-ex. Decision: keep public method names identical (send, close, stream) and add an explicit 'transport' keyword param on top-level Client constructors for clarity. Backcompat shim will warn on deprecated kwargs. Consensus: deprecate old kwarg names but do NOT remove in same minor release.

2026-03-06: Began JS implementation; found divergence in how streaming cancellation is surfaced. Trade-off: normalize on an AbortController-based pattern in JS and implement thin adapter in Python/Go shims for parity. Recorded in design doc.

2026-03-08: First interop test run across python/js/go against runtime-1.19 staging: streaming parity failures for edge-case multi-attachment prompts. Root cause: previous JS transport attached metadata frames differently. Fix landed in JS PR and validated locally.
2026-03-10: PRs opened for each repo. Requested reviews from codeowners and perf team. Added CI job to run cross-language golden tests on every transport change.
notes: Rollout plan: publish staggered SDK minor releases (py 1.12.x, js 2.6.x, go 0.10.x) with compatibility shims enabled by default. After one minor release and customer telemetry lookback, flip shim to opt-in and send an automated deprecation email. Rollback: revert PRs and re-publish previous artifact versions; CI prevents shipping if cross-lang golden tests fail.
qa_plan: Add new CI matrix entries exercising: short/long streaming, streaming cancelation, retry on 429/503, per-request metadata propagation. Run synthetic load for 24h on staging cluster to surface KV cache interactions. Invite 3 pilot customers to opt into beta release and collect logs for two weeks.
open_questions: Should we bump minimum supported Node version to 18 to reliably use AbortController across environments? (impact: some customers on 16)
Do we provide an automated codemod for common frameworks (FastAPI, Express, Gin) to update constructors?
What is the deprecation window for the old transport kwargs (one minor vs. two minors)?
